results.title: STORI Reviews (2026) | Product Hunt
results.content: of their app is to always "sell it" as a beta feature while offering in-app editing tools for real imagery as the selling point, because AI-powered imagery doesn't meet customers' expectations yet. About AI-powered text, to the contrary, there's really good prompting behind this app, and with a bit of manual editing here and there one can really save time and money. That makes it a worthy app with great potential, to me; one that I will use for some of my side projects, and whose evolution I'll certainly keep an eye on. 👀 Definitely supporting it. [...] the 3 dots on the CONTENT page. It makes perfect sense, don't misunderstand me, but whenever one step can be saved I'd always go for that. All the above don't affect my rating because it is expected to have terrain for improvement at launch, especially when it comes to UI and documentation. The issue I have is with AI-powered imagery: that technology is still far away from being usable in apps like this, because the results are awful. Those of Stori AI are not even that bad, but still not viable for branding, in my opinion. Thing is that this is a common problem to all similar apps right now, so I don't feel like it is a flaw of this particular app. My suggestion to anybody offering this kind of tech in an automated way as a feature of their app is to always "sell it" as a beta feature [...] What I absolutely loved : The simplicity of the UX and the seamlessness with which STORI AI almost accurately nails one's brand, and helps one navigate between different social media channels to see how their posts will appear. I have started using STORI AI to plan my content for different channels. 😊 Some challenges I am facing: 1. Whenever I try to edit AI generated text for my posts and hit save, the changes do not really reflect on my posts. I then keep on trying the same thing multiple times until it does finally actually save my changes and modifies my created content too. 2. The image is created solely in accordance to the text prompt we provide. Is it possible to have a separate AI generator for images where one can provide more detailed prompts on how they want the image to look
